key_insight: Ceramics are performance-engineered by controlling bonding, processing, and microstructure, but their brittleness and flaw sensitivity remain the central design constraint.
engineering_relevance: The paper connects processing routes and defect control to mechanical, thermal, electrical, and biomedical performance, making it directly relevant to ceramic design, manufacturing, and reliability engineering.
method: Compares conventional sintering, sol–gel processing, and additive manufacturing
Covers biomedical ceramics, nanoceramics, composites, and emerging defect-engineering strategies
evidence_signal: This is a review paper synthesizing reported relationships and trends rather than presenting new experimental data or a single evaluation dataset.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is the persistent porosity–strength trade-off, especially when scaling up manufacturing or using heterogeneous additive processes.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
